state.incidentInput: Customers are seeing errors at checkout and the site feels slow. Started maybe 15–20 min ago.
state.summary: Resolved (USER-003). CFG-502 (inventory DB_POOL_MAX 20->80, confirmed by the owner in USER-001) over-committed orders-db and starved orders-service, which caused the checkout errors. The revert at 14:35 restored connections to 250 and errors to 0.3% (USER-002). The payments latency rise (MET-payments.p95_latency_ms, LOG-046) was a symptom of checkout retries. Order reconciliation and prevention work remain.
state.impact: Onset 13:55, resolved after the 14:35 revert (USER-002, USER-003). Checkout errors peaked at 7.9% and orders errors at 10.3%. CUST-001: 87 tickets. CUST-002: 14 reports of cards charged with no order confirmation, which still need reconciling. Search and browsing were unaffected (CUST-004).

state.stakeholderUpdate: The incident is resolved. Checkout is working normally after we reverted a configuration change that let one internal service take too many database connections, and the change owner confirmed it was the cause. Support is still reconciling the orders where customers were charged without a confirmation. We are planning permanent safeguards to stop this recurring.

Confidence fairly high but not human-confirmed.
